Grok To Media Man Australia

Media Man Australia is an Australian media, publicity, advertising, online publishing, and project management company based in Sydney (operating across areas like Maroubra Beach, Bondi, Newport Beach, and Palm Beach).

Media Man Australia forms part of the Media Man Group, established in 2001 by media entrepreneur Greg Tingle (often referred to as "Media Man").

The group includes entities like Media Man Australia, Media Man Int, Australian Sports Entertainment, Casino News Media, Bitcoin News Media, Eastern Suburbs Media, and others focused on niche publishing and services.

Key Focus Areas

Services: Publicity/PR campaigns, online advertising (text links, banners, etc.), SEO/SEM, content creation, website promotion, brand exposure, and project management.

They target niches like sports/entertainment (especially pro wrestling/combat sports), gaming/iGaming, pop culture, Bitcoin/crypto, tourism, and local Australian news.

Content: News articles, feature interviews (e.g., with wrestlers like Ken Shamrock, Dallas Page), profiles, multimedia, market updates, and monthly "awards" for sites, wrestlers, businesses, etc. Heavy coverage of WWE, UFC, movies, streaming, Google/SEO topics, and beach/local Sydney culture.

Media Man Group SEO

Media Man Group SEO refers to the Search Engine Optimization services, strategies, and content produced by the Media Man Group (including Media Man Int / Media Man International and Media Man Australia), founded in 2001 by Greg Tingle in Sydney, Australia.

Overview

The Media Man Group is a media, publicity, advertising, online publishing, and project management company with a strong focus on SEO (often playfully called “Hunt Machine Optimisation” by Greg Tingle). They have developed effective SEO techniques since launch, helping their own sites achieve Hitwise Australia “Top 10” status in the entertainment/personalities category.

https://t.co/MtxsUIBop2

They integrate SEO with PR, content marketing, niche publishing, link-building, and authority projects for sustainable, white-hat results. Their approach emphasizes organic growth over paid ads alone, adapting to Google’s evolving algorithms (including AI Overviews, Helpful Content updates, and Core Web Vitals).

Services Offered

Media Man Group provides:

SEO and content marketing — Keyword research, on-page optimization, evergreen/high-quality content creation, and topical authority building.

Online advertising and link strategies — Text link campaigns, niche media placement, and authority-building projects.

Integrated publicity — Combining SEO with PR, press releases, social media buzz, and brand exposure (often via their network of niche sites like wrestling, gaming, and entertainment portals).

Technical and adaptive SEO — Site structure, crawlability, mobile-friendliness, adaptation to AI search, and monitoring via Google Search Console.  Niche and local SEO — Tailored for sectors like pop culture, combat sports/wrestling, gaming, business, and entertainment.

They position SEO as part of broader “Putting Your Name (and Brand) Out There” campaigns, using their own platforms as case studies.

Greg Tingle’s SEO Philosophy (“Hunt Machine Optimisation”)

Greg Tingle (founder and lead) is a longtime SEO practitioner with 25+ years of experience. His practical, ethical, user-first approach includes:

High-quality, valuable content — Unique, evergreen, audience-focused material that serves user intent (“Do-Know-Go” queries) and builds E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness).

Technical foundations — Clean site structure, fast loading (Core Web Vitals), proper metadata, internal linking, and crawlability.

Authority and links — Quality backlinks via PR, content, and relationships rather than spammy tactics.

Adaptation to modern search — Monitoring Google updates, AI Overviews, conversational queries, and generative search. Focus on helpful content over keyword stuffing.

Sustainable organic growth — Organic SEO for long-term results, often outperforming or complementing paid ads.

He shares insights via blogs, X, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube, frequently summarizing Google’s Search Off The Record podcast and other updates.

Key Strategies They Promote

From their sites and posts:

Keyword research — Target relevant, long-tail, and intent-based keywords; use tools like Google Keyword Planner or similar.

On-page SEO — Natural keyword use in titles, meta descriptions, headings, URLs, alt text, and content.

Content strategy — Create original, high-quality, regularly updated content; build topical authority in niches.

Technical SEO — Ensure mobile-friendliness, speed, proper indexing (monitor Search Console), and avoid issues like soft 404s or blocking.

Off-page and authority — Earn quality links, leverage PR/media placements, and build E-E-A-T signals. AI-era adaptation — Optimize for featured snippets, rich results, and AI Overviews; focus on user value and semantic relevance.  Monitoring and iteration — Use Google Search Console, Analytics, and track SERPs; test changes and monitor trends.

They often cover topics like indexing reports, Markdown vs. HTML for AI, lazy loading, and small business SEO.

Their SEO Content and Activity

Media Man Group actively produces and shares SEO resources:

Dedicated sections like SEO News and Search Engine Optimization pages on https://t.co/MtxsUIBop2 and related sites.

Frequent X posts summarizing Google updates, Search Off The Record episodes, and practical tips.

Monthly awards and spotlights that include “Search Engine Of The Month” (often Google).

Case studies through their own optimized network of sites (wrestling, markets, pop culture, etc.).

Their content is practical, gonzo-style journalism mixed with actionable advice, often tying SEO to publicity and niche media.

Summary

Media Man Group treats SEO as a core, integrated service alongside publicity and content creation.

Their long track record, focus on ethical/white-hat tactics, and adaptation to AI/search changes make them a niche player especially strong in entertainment, sports, and Australian/digital media sectors.

The model humans prefer the most is not always the most accurate one!

Arena just added factuality scoring to their leaderboard alongside human preference. The idea: human preference measures whether a response felt good to read. Factuality measures the correctness of claims in a model's response. These are two different things.

Most benchmarks test models on fixed, predetermined questions in a lab setting. What Arena is doing differently: measuring factuality in real, open-ended user conversations at scale.

Over 2 million claims extracted from actual conversations, verified against the web, across 130k Text Arena battles and 40k Search Arena battles.

The way it works: they randomly sample battles, extract web-verifiable claims from each model response, verify them against the web, and calculate a factuality score per model. The final ranking is a weighted combination of human preference and factuality score.

When factuality weight is enabled, the shifts are significant. In Text Arena, GPT-5.5 jumps 13 spots. Muse Spark drops 13. Claude Fable 5 moves down slightly. In Search Arena, GPT-5.5-search takes the top spot while Gemini grounding drops from 7 to 13.
